subject: Post-call: Model-fit & prompt collection for ACME
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>, Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Model-fit & prompt collection for ACME

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and next steps from our discovery call: 

- Objective: ACME wants an API-backed summarization + extraction workflow for customer support tickets (multi-turn). Primary goals are 90th‑pct latency < 300ms and F1 > 0.85 on entity extraction.
- Data characteristics: average ticket length ~600 tokens, 5–10 languages (EN primary), high PII density (emails, order numbers).
- Constraints: must support SOC2 evidence for redaction, and allow on-prem/private deployment for EU PHI later in the year.

Proposed next steps (helpful if you can confirm by EOD Wednesday):
1) Share an initial prompt set (edge cases + typical examples). We prefer CSV with columns: prompt_id, input_example, expected_output, category, notes. I attached a template (prompt_collection_template.csv).
2) Redaction guidance: please flag any PII fields and indicate whether you can accept us redacting or we should handle. We'll send a short redaction guidance doc once you confirm.
3) Model recommendations & evals: based on the call, our recommended starting points are rw-ember-2 (latency-optimized) for low-latency summarization and rw-llm-13b-quant (cost-optimized, 4-bit) for high-quality extraction. We can run a benchmark with your prompts — see the benchmark summary attached.
4) Logistics: share sample prompts by email or upload to the Drive link below; once we have them we'll schedule a 1‑week batch of eval runs and share a result dashboard.

Attachments: prompt_collection_template.csv, benchmark-summary-acme.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow if anything needs clarifying.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model-fit & prompt collection for ACME

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the template. A few quick items from our side:

- We'll start with a subset of 200 tickets (anonymized) to test extraction. Can you confirm whether the evaluation can run on our data in a private Dedicated pool? We need to understand isolation/retention.
- Redaction: we typically replace emails and order numbers with [REDACTED_ORDER] / [REDACTED_EMAIL], but we have a couple of edge cases where the order number format varies significantly. Any guidance on how you want those represented in the expected_output column would help.

I've attached a small sample of prompts and expected outputs (acme_sample_prompts.csv) to illustrate the format. Sample rows included inline below for quick reference:

"prompt_id","input_example","expected_output","category","notes"
"SMP-001","Customer: My order 123-XY failed. Pls refund","{\"order_id\": \"123-XY\", \"intent\": \"refund_request\"}","extraction","order id with dash"
"SMP-002","Agent: Please confirm your email -> john.doe@example.com","{\"email\": \"[REDACTED_EMAIL]\"}","redaction","redacted emails in output"

Two questions for you: 1) Are we okay to send these 200 tickets via SFTP to a Dedicated evaluation environment? 2) What does the benchmark dashboard look like (metrics, per-prompt traces)?

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel
Director, Customer Support Tech
Acme Corp
sam.patel@acme.com

Attachment: acme_sample_prompts.csv

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model-fit & prompt collection for ACME

Thanks Sam — great sample, and those two sample rows are exactly the shape we need. Quick answers and guidance: 

1) Private Dedicated pool: yes, we can run the eval on a Dedicated environment with isolated storage and automatic post-run purge. I'll loop in our Security PO to confirm retention windows, but baseline is 30 days with the option to shorten on request.

2) SFTP for the 200 tickets is fine — please upload to the ACME eval bucket (we'll give SFTP creds). If you prefer to push via the Drive folder that's OK as well.

3) Redaction guidance (high level):
- Replace PII with deterministic tokens in inputs only (e.g., [REDACTED_EMAIL], [REDACTED_ORDER]).
- In expected_output, prefer the canonical token for entity fields (e.g., "order_id": "[REDACTED_ORDER]") so the eval matches cleanly.
- For order number format variance, include multiple representative examples in the prompt set and add a note (category: edge_case). We treat edge cases as a separate slice in the dashboard so we can track regressions.

4) Benchmark dashboard: the default dashboard includes per-prompt-level traces, token latency distributions (p50/p90/p99), extraction F1 by entity type, and an edge-case slice. We'll share a live report link after the run; summary metrics are included in benchmark-summary-acme.pdf. Example metrics: p90 latency = 280ms on rw-ember-2; extraction F1 = 0.87 (rw-llm-13b-quant) on our initial open-source baseline.

Next actions from Redwood:
- I'll send SFTP credentials and a short redaction-guidelines.pdf (attached).
- We'll schedule a 1-week eval window starting as soon as you upload the prompts and data. Please confirm preferred start date (we can do as soon as Tue 2026-07-14).

If you'd like, Logan can coordinate the eval run and share the dashboard.

Best,
Marissa
(Account Executive)

Attachments: redaction-guidelines.pdf

---

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model-fit & prompt collection for ACME

Looping in on the execution details — Marissa, I'll own the eval run. Proposed plan:
- Start Tue 2026-07-14, run for 7 days against both rw-ember-2 (low-latency) and rw-llm-13b-quant (quality/cost tradeoff).
- We'll upload per-prompt traces to the shared Drive folder and give you a live dashboard link with slices for "edge_case", "redaction", and "multilingual".
- If ACME needs on-prem later, we'll provide the same eval artifacts and an exportable report (PDF + raw CSVs).

Sam — can you confirm SFTP or Drive for upload and confirm 200-ticket subset by EOD Monday? Once confirmed I'll provision the Dedicated pool and share creds.
